question: Why did Hans Albert name an ancient argument for doubting every justification after Baron Münchhausen?
answer: Because escaping it means pulling yourself out of a swamp by your own hair, as the baron claimed to have done. Every reason needs a reason: the chain runs on forever, circles back, or stops at a claim simply laid down. Albert named it in 1968; Sextus had listed the same exits.
move: Every chain of reasons ends somewhere; know where yours stops and why.
ask: Where does my reasoning for an important belief stop, and why there?
reference: Albert, Treatise on Critical Reason, trans. Rorty, Princeton University Press, 1985 (German original 1968)
